text:
Maya R: Heads up — noticed a latency regression on mistral-16b-awq-int8 after yesterday's kernel selector tweak. 50-120ms tail increase on hf-infer workloads.
Derek: ugh, saw a couple alerts. can you paste the perf trace?
Maya R: pasted initial flame: 
``` 
# perf top snippet
cpu cycles  |  kernel_mistral_awq_selector
cpu cycles  |  kv_prefetch_worker
cpu cycles  |  rope_scale_adjust
```
Maya R: Looks like KV hotpath is contending with rope scaling path. selector now prefers an FP8-ish kernel in some sequences, fallback to int8 when rope_scale > 1.0 — that's thrashing cache.
Sam: can you repro locally with bench-run? I can run microbench on the head/kv dims.
Maya R: repro script attached: `./tools/bench.sh --model mistral-16b --quant awq-int8 --seq 1024 --concurrency 8 --profile`
Eve: quick note — the telemetry shows a spike in KV eviction rate after the selector change. eviction rate went from 0.6% -> 4.8% for hot keys.
Derek: is this specific to AWQ? have we seen it on gptq or fp8 builds?
Maya R: AWQ-int8 and gptq-int8 both show regression but AWQ path hits the fallback in more cases because kernel selection uses estimated error budget vs rope scale. FP8 path wasn't touched by this selector.
Sam: i'll run a bisect between kernels. plan: (1) baseline old selector (A), (2) new selector (B), (3) force kernel=legacy-int8 (C). compare p50/p95/p99 and kv-evict rate.
Maya R: good. also please include a short calibration prompt set — calibration prompts we used for AWQ: ["Please summarize:", "Translate to French:", "Write a short email:"] — those are sensitive to quant deltas.
infra-bot: scheduled bench job #3456 on infra-cluster-3 (owner: Sam)
Sam: results from run #3456:
``` 
A: p50=84ms p95=120ms p99=215ms kv-evict=0.7% throughput=180 tps
B: p50=90ms p95=210ms p99=410ms kv-evict=4.5% throughput=140 tps
C: p50=86ms p95=125ms p99=230ms kv-evict=0.9% throughput=175 tps
```
Sam: conclusion: new selector (B) increases p99 massively and raises kv-evict. forcing legacy-int8 (C) recovers almost entirely.
Derek: sounds like selector misestimates cost of rope-rescale branch and chooses a kernel that requires extra prefetching or bigger kv entries. any hotpatch ideas?
Maya R: quick mitigation: add a cheap heuristic — if rope_scale > 1.1 and model in {mistral-16b, mixtral-8x} prefer legacy-int8 kernel. avoids fallback churn. Long term: add dynamic cost model using sampled latency stats per-kernel per-seqlen.
Eve: can we also tighten KV cache admission limits briefly to stop eviction storms while we roll the heuristic?
Sam: yes, prepping a rollout: canary 5% traffic with heuristic, monitor kv-evict, p99 and generation errors (accuracy).
Maya R: note on accuracy — AWQ calibration diffs for those prompts: BLEU-like delta ~ -0.7% vs baseline on the sample set when forcing legacy-int8. acceptable for now.
Derek: create PR for heuristic + rollout config and include runbook steps (how to revert kernel selector). I can review.
Maya R: PR opened: https://git.redwood/repo/infra/merge/1892 — includes telemetry to track kernel-choice, kv-evict, rope_scale histograms.
Eve: added alerting rule draft: trigger when kv-evict > 3% AND p99 > 300ms for 5m.
Sam: I'll kick off the canary later today and post results. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
Derek: thanks — if canary is clean we can bake into next patch release.
infra-bot: canary job #3470 queued (5% traffic)
Sam: canary results (after 30m): p99 down to 220ms, kv-evict 0.95%, no increase in calibration error. rolling to 25%.
Maya R: rolling notes added to runbook. closing thread after full rollout.
